## 固定收益開場論點

美國與伊朗達成臨時協議，帶動油價大幅下跌，政策敏感型殖利率盤中一度明顯回落，但美債6月15日收盤僅小幅上漲。2年期殖利率下跌1.3個基點至4.069%，5年期下跌1.5個基點至4.192%，10年期下降0.6個基點至4.475%；30年期則逆勢上升1.2個基點至4.98%，使2s30s曲線陡化2.5個基點至91.1個基點。

收盤變動有限，掩蓋了盤中幅度更大的重新定價。交易員將聯準會在12月前升息的機率，從前一週已完全反映降至不足80%，2年期殖利率一度大跌7個基點至4.01%，10年期也曾觸及4.42%。其後兩者回吐大部分走勢，因投資人開始區分原油即時下跌、協議執行仍有不確定性，以及已在經濟中傳導的通膨壓力。

美國與伊朗表示已達成停止戰爭並重開荷莫茲海峽的臨時協議，預定6月19日在瑞士正式簽署，隨後就德黑蘭核計畫展開為期60天的談判。WTI收跌4.87%至$80.75，布蘭特原油下跌4.76%至$83.17，降低了央行未來面臨的能源衝擊。不過，雙方尚未公布共同確認的協議文本，航運也未恢復正常，伊朗並提出涉及凍結資金、制裁及海上封鎖的條件。

美國數據支持聯準會本週暫緩行動，卻未解除通膨疑慮。6月紐約州製造業指數由19.6降至5.7，遠低於12.5至14.0的預期區間；5月工業生產僅增長0.1%，不及0.2%的市場共識，製造業產出持平，也未達預期的0.3%增幅。然而，該地區調查的支付價格指數仍高達61.0，供應取得情況惡化，製造商並預期未來6個月售價漲幅將加快。

這組訊號解釋了油價下跌之際，美債漲勢為何仍逐步消退。10年期實質殖利率下降1.4個基點至2.137%，但10年期損益兩平通膨率上升0.8個基點至2.338%。因此，名目殖利率回落源自實質殖利率下降，而非長期通膨補償再度大幅下滑。長端同樣抗拒漲勢；即使短端反映聯準會升息的急迫性下降，10年期以遠仍呈現溫和的熊市陡峭化。

風險資產對眼前最壞能源情境消退的反應更為強烈。標普500指數上漲1.65%，那斯達克100指數上漲3.06%，費城半導體指數大漲5.45%；VIX下跌8.37%至16.2，美元指數則下滑0.12%。信用市場順利承接大量發行，其中以Nvidia的$250億債券最受矚目，訂單一度高達$850億。這正是本交易日的核心對比：協議提振風險承擔意願並降低近期緊縮壓力，卻不足以使美債投資人相信通膨衝擊及其政策後果已完全逆轉。

## 荷莫茲協議消除尾部風險，執行風險仍在

這項外交宣布改變了未來能源前景，卻未真正解決根本爭端。臨時協議旨在重開荷莫茲海峽並停止戰事，核問題則留待60天談判期處理。美國與伊朗官員預定6月19日在瑞士簽署協議；美國總統川普表示，海峽將於當日完成除雷後重新開放。

市場反應凸顯這條水道對全球能源供應的重要性。戰爭爆發前，全球約五分之一的海運石油與液化天然氣，以及約三分之一的肥料出口均經由荷莫茲海峽運輸。海峽關閉造成供應衝擊，推升成熟及新興經濟體的通膨數據、航運成本與央行升息預期。若能重開，將直接有助原油價格與進口成本下降，並減輕整體通膨壓力。

實際作業障礙仍相當可觀。據報近600艘船隻受困波斯灣，另有數百艘在海灣外等待。僅除雷作業就可能耗時30天，即使恢復通航，受損的能源基礎設施也可能延後供應回升。德黑蘭表示，通行海峽的船舶將由伊朗與阿曼共同管理，意味伊朗對通行權的控制仍屬談判內容，而非已完全解決的問題。

兩國政府對擴大談判展開前必須滿足的條件，也提出不同說法。伊朗半官方的梅爾通訊社報導，除非伊朗一半的凍結資金獲得解凍、石油制裁暫停且海上封鎖解除，否則最終談判不會展開。美國解除制裁可能還需要國會批准。德黑蘭也試圖將停火與以色列和黎巴嫩真主黨的衝突掛鉤，另增一項超出美伊雙邊爭端的條件。

這些懸而未決的條款，解釋了利率收盤變動遠小於盤中極值的原因。油價下降降低了成熟市場必須積極緊縮的預期，但協議仍只是一套框架，其通膨效果取決於實際船運、能源供應與政治履約。川普表示，若核談判失敗，軍事攻擊可能恢復；伊朗強硬派與以色列的反對態度，也為協議破裂增添其他可能路徑。

美債收盤曲線反映的正是這種附帶條件的利多。眼前的變化是市場認為聯準會升息機率下降，因此短天期債券表現較佳。2年期殖利率早盤降至4.01%，其後收於4.069%；主要附息債券天期中，5年期的單日降幅最大。10年期收盤僅下降0.6個基點，30年期則上升。

2s10s曲線陡化0.7個基點至40.6個基點，2s30s擴大2.5個基點至91.1個基點。這種走勢並不代表市場重新湧現對長天期債券的避險需求，而是投資人削減短端部分政策緊縮溢價，同時仍要求長端提供補償，以承擔殘留的通膨、供給與期限風險。

重新定價期間，美債現券交易相當活躍。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$9,721億、共319,747筆，較6月12日增加8.9%；名目附息債交易量增加3.6%至$7,604億。20年期以上天期的交易量增加35%至$841億，5年以上至7年期區間則增長25.3%至$644億。這些數據無法判定投資方向，但顯示收盤變動雖小，背後成交相當可觀，尤其集中在最能反映當日矛盾的天期：政策風險降低，長端卻持續抗拒上漲。

跨資產反應則更明確偏向樂觀。科技股領漲，高收益債與新興市場債券基金也小幅上揚。黃金仍上漲2.68%至$4,328，顯示股市走高並未消除防禦性資產需求。美元小幅下跌與避險需求減弱一致，但相較油價與科技股的走勢仍相當克制。

因此，協議改變的是各種結果的機率分布，而非為地緣政治事件畫下句點。持續發生嚴重供應中斷的可能性有所降低，央行也取得更多觀望空間，但能源流量多快恢復正常、制裁能否解除，以及60天是否足以解決核爭端，都還沒有答案。對債市而言，下一階段的關鍵在於期貨價格急跌，能否轉化為實際交付的能源價格及更廣泛通膨持續下降。

## 聯準會會前：生產轉弱，價格壓力仍具黏性

6月紐約州製造業調查清楚顯示製造動能轉弱。整體企業狀況指數由19.6降至5.7，低於12.5至14.0的預期區間；新訂單由22.7放緩至3.5，出貨由18.9降至8.6，顯示總指數轉弱源自當前活動普遍降溫，而非單一分項拖累。

就業形成對照。員工人數指數由8.3升至9.6，顯示即使訂單與出貨放緩，企業仍在增聘人員。預期也維持正向，6個月企業狀況指數僅由33.5降至30.1。這份調查指向成長放慢，而非製造業直接陷入萎縮。

價格與供應指標對聯準會而言較不令人放心。支付價格指數由62.6微降至61.0，但仍處高檔；收取價格指數也僅由31.8降至31.4。供應取得指數由負10.7惡化至負13.9。更重要的是，作為前瞻通膨訊號的未來6個月預期收取價格指數，由43.6升至51.6。

5月工業生產也強化活動趨緩的訊息。總產出月增0.1%，低於0.2%的市場共識；4月增幅則由0.7%上修至0.9%。相較去年同期，產出增長1.7%。月度疲弱主要集中在製造業：4月增幅上修至0.7%後，5月產出持平，不及增長0.3%的預期。

不過，各產業表現使這份報告不能被視為全面疲弱的明確訊號。礦業產出增長1.3%，企業設備增加0.6%，營建用品上升1.1%，公用事業則下降0.4%。產能利用率由76.1%升至符合預期的76.2%，製造業利用率持平於75.7%。經濟產出低於預期的月度增速，但利用率數據並未顯示閒置產能突然擴大。

整體而言，這些數據給予聯準會先觀察、而非立即行動的理由。成長動能不如5月就業報告及先前支出數據所暗示的強勁，油價回落也改善了未來整體通膨路徑。然而，支付價格高企、供應取得惡化及預期售價漲幅上升，均說明決策者不能因產出放緩，便推斷通膨問題已經結束。

市場定價也朝這個方向調整。交易員將12月前升息1碼的機率降至約74%，直到2027年3月才完全反映一次升息。瑞銀策略師Leslie Falconio表示，油價下跌讓市場得以撤除先前加入的部分升息定價，並協助2年期殖利率下降。她仍預期FOMC本週會取消寬鬆傾向，但繼續預測下一次實際利率變動將是2027年降息。

當前決策與政策傾向之間的區別至關重要。市場普遍預期，Kevin Warsh首次以聯準會主席身分主持會議時，利率將維持在3.50%至3.75%。最新數據使本週升息的可能性偏低，但委員會仍須決定是否暗示下一步可能朝任一方向調整。油價下跌降低緊急收緊政策的必要性；調查中的價格黏性及仍具韌性的產能利用率，則不支持重新明確偏向寬鬆。

國庫券標售另提供了短端需求訊號。$890.01億的13週期國庫券以3.640%的最高得標利率決標，與前一週相同。投標倍數由2.79降至2.47，間接投標人獲配49.81%，直接投標人獲配4.77%，一級交易商承接45.42%。交易商獲配比例升高並伴隨投標倍數明顯轉弱，但由於沒有發行前交易殖利率可供比較，無法判斷決標本身是否出現尾差。

$770億的26週期國庫券標售結果較穩健。最高得標利率為3.680%，較前一週低1個基點，投標倍數則由2.75微升至2.76。間接投標人獲配70.11%，直接投標人6.57%，交易商23.33%。兩檔證券均於6月18日交割，但需求結構差異明顯，不宜將兩場標售視為單一且一致的短端流動性判斷。

13週期國庫券在利率不變下顯示承接較弱；26週期國庫券則維持投標倍數，並以略低利率吸引遠高得多的間接投標比例。兩場標售都未顯示普遍性的融資壓力，真正的訊息在於市場分化：聯準會會議、企業繳稅日及密集美債交割到來前，6個月期的現金需求環境較3個月期更為寬鬆。

## Nvidia巨額發債考驗AI信用需求深度

企業借款人積極利用市場情緒改善，Nvidia則完成本交易日最具代表性的信用交易。這家晶片製造商售出$250億投資級債券，是2021年以來首次發債；在獲得最高$850億訂單後，發行規模由最初約$200億的目標上調。

本次發行分為7個天期，涵蓋2年至30年。行銷期間，最長天期券的定價收窄25個基點，最終以高於美債65個基點定價。Nvidia未舉行大型高評級債券發行通常會有的投資人說明會，便完成交易，反映其市場領導地位、強勁信用評等，以及身為債券發行人的稀缺性。

Nvidia的財務結構也有別於槓桿較高的AI基礎設施借款人。依分析師平均預估，截至1月31日止的會計年度，公司自由現金流可望超過$2,000億。Nvidia既是Alphabet、Amazon等科技公司資料中心擴建的主要供應商，也透過投資Intel、Anthropic及OpenAI配置自身資本。

募集資金部分將用於再融資既有債務。成本相對低廉的長天期資金也能支持策略投資與股東回饋，而不致實質削弱Nvidia的AA信用體質。因此，投資人所融資的，既是一項龐大的資本配置計畫，也是一家內部現金創造能力格外強勁的公司。

整體市場也展現相似的承接能力。週一共有8家投資級發行人籌得$360億。衡量投資級信用風險的一項指標降至2月初以來最低，也就是伊朗衝突爆發前的水準；美國高評級債券基金則已連續13個月錄得資金流入。油價下降、美債殖利率溫和回落，加上基金需求持續，共同造就格外有利的發行窗口。

但強大承接能力並未消除集中風險。Nvidia的交易加入了數千億美元投入資料中心及其他AI基礎設施的科技業借款。摩根士丹利債務資本市場主管估計，今年所有信用債發行中，與AI相關的比重可能高達15%，儘管這類發行在2年前幾乎不存在。

這項轉變除了反映在初級市場行事曆，也開始出現在總體資產負債表。Bespoke Investment Group發現，過去一年，美國GDP每增加一單位所伴隨的債務增長量已經上升，企業借款是這項變化的核心。AI投資有助解釋經濟成長、進口與債券發行為何都變得更加仰賴信用。這些融資能在最終生產力效益實現前先支持產出，但也更凸顯那些效益能否足以負擔新增資本成本。

Nuveen的Laura Parrott管理約$750億投資級債券投資組合，採取的作法更具選擇性。她著重於為AI提供電力、輸配電及其他周邊基礎設施的能源和公用事業信用債，而非只押注最終勝出的科技企業。她也警告，超大規模雲端業者、模型開發商與基礎設施供應商之間的循環關係，可能使投資組合對同一實質借款人的曝險，高於各筆交易名稱所顯示的程度。

其他初級市場交易顯示，需求並不局限於美國科技業。蒙特婁的都會快速交通系統Réseau express métropolitain，透過5年、7年、10年與30年期債券籌得C$18.5億。30年期券以高於政府公債95個基點定價，殖利率為4.791%，訂單超過發行規模5倍。這筆融資使先前投入輕軌專案的資金得以重新配置；不過，整套系統預計要等機場連線於2027年開通後才能全面營運，專案估計成本也已由2015年至今幾乎倍增至C$94億。

Waste Management of Canada以高於政府公債72個基點的利差，售出C$7億7年期債券，較初步定價收窄3個基點。Birkenstock另準備發行€9億7年期債券，3年後可贖回，這將是公司自2021年以來首次發債。這家鞋類公司計畫將資金用於債務再融資，並可能拿出最高$5億進一步回購股票；此前已完成$2.5億加速股票回購。

有利的發行環境也讓世界銀行旗下民營部門機構得以擴大較不傳統的融資架構。國際金融公司不到一年內完成第2筆新興市場擔保貸款憑證，籌得$5.09億，使整項計畫規模超過$10億。交易涵蓋來自南美洲、中東、北非及亞洲的62筆美元計價貸款。

其中$3.2億優先順位分券獲穆迪暫定Aaa評等，以高於SOFR 120個基點定價，較國際金融公司首筆交易的同類分券收窄10個基點。這項架構把部分貸款機構風險移轉給債券投資人，釋出資本以承作新貸款，同時為買方提供分散的新興市場曝險。定價收窄直接顯示投資人對該架構已更加熟悉。

同一波市場強勢也促使監管機關更加關注透明度較低的信用管道。歐洲央行已將銀行與私人信貸關係的審查範圍，由約12家機構擴大至20多家。有重大曝險的銀行將須每年提供資料；官員不僅檢視放款金額，也關注基金、被投資公司與共同放款安排之間的重疊曝險。

根據彭博產業研究，德意志銀行、巴克萊、法國巴黎銀行與匯豐合計占歐洲銀行私人信貸曝險近三分之二。已揭露曝險約占貸款的2.3%，顯示整體規模仍可管理，但歐洲央行監管人員擔心，若未妥善彙總曝險，壓力時期的集中度及相關性可能遭到掩蓋。在私人信貸基金限制贖回、投資人信心轉弱之後，這項審查尤其值得關注。

信用市場因而呈現當前需求充沛、結構性集中度卻日益升高的局面。投資人認為Nvidia的資產負債表、發行稀缺性及AI生態系地位格外強勁，因此公司得以擴大發行規模並顯著收窄定價。歐洲央行的審查與Nuveen對集中度的疑慮，則反映同一融資熱潮的另一面：市場可以在利差未立即承壓時吸收龐大供給，但仍可能累積彼此連結的曝險；只有當成長、流動性或預期中的AI回報不如預期時，這些關係才會浮現。

## 歐洲在產出疲弱與能源二輪效應間權衡

歐洲利率市場同樣受惠於油價下跌，但央行官員不認為能源期貨價格下跌，就代表已在經濟中傳導的通膨壓力已經逆轉。歐洲央行總裁拉加德表示，高能源價格的間接影響已開始廣泛浮現；是否需要進一步行動，將取決於基礎通膨與薪資壓力。

歐洲央行前一週將存款利率上調25個基點，是2023年以來首次升息。貨幣市場仍反映年底前再升息1碼至2.5%，但進一步升至2.75%的機率已由前一週完全反映，降至約25%。這項重新定價承認，荷莫茲海峽若能持久重開，將降低快速連續升息的必要性，卻不會抹除先前衝擊的影響。

拉加德對可能達成的協議表示歡迎，但強調能否落實取決於未來數日發展、正式簽署備忘錄，以及海峽實際重開與完成除雷。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel警告，石油供應可能需要數月才能恢復正常；隨著能源帳單的財政補助到期，通膨壓力還可能再度上升。

歐洲央行管理委員會其他成員對所需政策速度看法不一。葡萄牙的Alvaro Santos Pereira表示，在官員確定通膨是否會從能源與肥料擴散至其他產業前，現在推斷政策路徑仍言之過早。斯洛伐克的Peter Kazimir主張將剩餘工作提前完成，理由是戰爭造成的經濟損害無法立即逆轉。拉脫維亞的Martins Kazaks則表示，若較高能源價格繼續擴散，歐洲央行已準備再次行動。

成長數據更支持審慎行事。歐元區4月工業生產月增0.1%，低於0.2%的市場共識，3月則增長0.4%；較去年同期增長0.3%，也不及0.4%的預期。中間財增長0.8%，耐久消費品增加1.0%，非耐久消費品增加1.7%；能源產出下降0.4%，資本財則減少0.5%。

產業組成顯示，消費相關生產維持穩健，資本財部門仍然疲弱。放眼整個歐盟，產出月增0.1%、年增0.9%。數據並未指向工業活動驟然萎縮，但在較高能源成本已由源頭向外傳導之際，歐元區成長動能仍相當有限。

歐洲信用市場面臨相同矛盾。德意志銀行策略師偏好美元公司債而非歐元信用債，因為他們預期戰爭後續影響將透過具黏性的通膨、較高航運成本、記憶體晶片短缺與關稅不確定性，對歐洲發行人造成更大壓力。他們預測歐元投資級債利差年底前將擴大近20個基點至95個基點，高收益債利差則擴大77個基點至345個基點。

相較之下，他們對美國的預測較溫和：投資級債利差擴大10個基點至82個基點，高收益債擴大39個基點。策略師認為歐洲單一B級企業尤其脆弱；若總融資成本增加0.5個百分點，其中44%將轉為負自由現金流。這項比較不代表市場正立即承壓，卻凸顯歐洲成長較弱、再融資能力較差時，油價下降帶來的緩解可能較不持久。

波蘭的政策討論轉向較不鷹派，但並未重新承諾寬鬆。貨幣政策委員會委員Ludwik Kotecki表示，利率可能至少維持3.75%至年底，甚至延續至2027年3月，屆時基期效應應會壓低年通膨率。戰爭推升能源價格後，該委員會已暫停降息循環。

Kotecki表示，臨時協議降低再次升息的可能性，尤其波蘭5月通膨已放緩至3.1%。但他仍反對暗示近期恢復降息。即使政府取消燃油價格上限後通膨上升，他也認為這將是行政措施造成的漲幅，且核心價格壓力仍低。他的立場使波蘭介於正積極討論升息的歐洲央行，與能夠立即寬鬆的央行之間。

辛巴威成為美伊協議公布後首個降息的央行，將基準利率由35%降至30%。央行總裁John Mushayavanhu表示，此舉是因應通膨結構性變化的重新校準，而非寬鬆循環的起點。年通膨率由4月的4.8%降至5月的4.4%，也已遠低於2025年7月的95.8%。央行預期石油與肥料運輸恢復將進一步支持通膨下降，但仍明確區分一次性調整與持續降息。

巴西則朝相反方向發展。即使決策者已連續降息1碼至14.5%，經濟學家仍將年底Selic利率預測由13.5%上調至13.75%。同一調查也將2027年底預估由11.5%提高至12%，2028年底預測則由10%升至10.25%。

2026年預期通膨由5.11%升至5.3%，高於央行3%的目標，也超過4.5%的容許區間上限。10月大選前的財政支持、巴西里拉走弱及潛在聖嬰現象影響，使價格風險在全球油價下跌之際仍然延續。這些證據令投資人懷疑，央行在即將召開的會議後是否仍有繼續降息的空間。

## 主權融資與亞洲流動性凸顯本地風險

全球風險偏好改善，為評等較低的主權及類主權借款人打開融資機會，但各自的財政與流動性條件仍是決定性因素。肯亞計畫在7月開始的會計年度發行$11.3億外債，作為5,290億肯亞先令外部借款計畫的一部分，用以填補相當於GDP 5.5%的赤字。

這筆債券、世界銀行發展政策貸款及非洲開發銀行融資，預計將提供肯亞近三分之二的外部資金。財政部預期世界銀行將撥付1,705億先令，非洲開發銀行則提供213億先令。國際貨幣基金將肯亞列為債務困境高風險國家；國會議員也警告，持續借款以支應預算開支及再融資，正在加重未來財政壓力。

這項擬議發行之前，肯亞已在2月完成$22.5億雙券交易，2025年進行$30億市場操作，並於2024年發行$15億6年期歐洲債券。這些交易延長了到期年限並減輕近期外部流動性壓力，但新債仍延續了部分仰賴市場融資管理既有債務的模式。

蘇格蘭則正準備性質不同的類主權首次發債。其權力下放政府計畫於2026年第4季或2027年第1季發行債券，啟動一項為期5年、總額£15億的計畫。這項交易將以直接從市場籌資的方式，取代部分向英國中央政府借款。

定價的核心問題是投資人將如何看待蘇格蘭最終可能獨立的風險。在現行憲政架構下，標普與穆迪給予蘇格蘭和英國相同評等，但兩者都明確指出，這項評估以蘇格蘭留在聯合王國為前提。投資人關注的是，若蘇格蘭獨立，債券是否仍以英鎊償還，以及文件是否會納入提前贖回條款。

目前向銀行提出的假設是，債券不會為重大政治事件設置特殊契約條款。可比標的的利差範圍很廣：曼島債券較同類英國公債高出逾50個基點，2060年到期的蘭開夏郡議會債券則有接近70個基點的溢酬。最終發行年期的重要性可能不亞於發行人當前評等，因為相較5年期券，30年期債券承受憲政變動的曝險要高得多。

台灣公債市場面臨的是更迫切的流動性問題。稅款繳納、通膨疑慮及券商貸款需求收緊資金情勢，使5年期公債殖利率接近2008年以來最高，10年期也逼近3年高點。券商為參與AI帶動的股市漲勢而借款，進一步加重銀行流動性壓力。

由於銀行保留現金、不願增購央行票券，未償央行定期存單已降至NT$6.15兆，是2010年6月以來最低。公債標售需求也已轉弱，前一週10年期標售殖利率創2013年以來最高。央行總裁楊金龍將債券及央行定期存單需求下降，歸因於繳稅、AI企業資金需求與股市熱潮。

市場預期台灣央行6月18日將把政策利率維持在2%，但投資人會觀察5月通膨超過央行警戒值後，政策指引是否改變。全球油價下降給予官員一些觀望空間，現有市場利率也已在抑制需求。法國巴黎銀行分析師提出一種可能性：央行逐步引導隔夜拆款利率向政策利率靠攏，藉此抑制投機性借款，而無須立即調高基準利率。

日本央行在6月15日至16日會議結束時，面臨不同的溝通挑戰。市場普遍預期利率將由約0.75%上調25個基點至1%，創1995年以來最高。由於總裁植田和男仍在住院，他將以書面提出意見但不參與表決，會後則由副總裁內田真一說明決策。

內田必須同時說明後續利率路徑及日本央行的債券購買計畫。市場預期央行將宣布，從2027年4月起停止削減購債，這是貨幣政策正常化計畫的一項重大變化。強硬的利率訊號可能支撐日圓，卻會加重日本公債市場的壓力；該市場原已難以吸引穩定的超長債買盤。若訊息偏審慎，又可能重新引發通膨與匯率疲弱速度超越政策調整的疑慮。

美國以外市場本日的整體啟示是，油價下降雖改善全球起點，卻不會導向一致的利率結果。辛巴威通膨放緩程度足以支持降息，波蘭有空間等待，巴西的財政與通膨結構壓縮寬鬆餘地，台灣債市壓力則同時來自國內現金短缺與能源價格。即使全球環境緩解，日本央行仍預期升息，因為其政策正常化、日圓與通膨條件各有不同。

## 後續市場意義

亞洲首波考驗於6月16日到來。中國將於上海時間10:00公布5月工業生產、零售銷售與固定資產投資。前值分別為工業生產年增4.1%、零售銷售增長3.2%，固定資產投資年初至今萎縮1.6%。在民間借款疲弱、銀行流動性充裕之際，這組數據將顯示內需是否正在復甦。

日本央行將在6月15日至16日會議後公布決策，市場預期升息25個基點至約1%。由於利率調整已獲充分預期，市場將更重視內田真一對後續升息及購債計畫的說明。若確認自2027年4月起停止削減購債，可能有助市場運作，但投資人也會評估這項決策是否改變貨幣政策正常化速度。

澳洲央行將於雪梨時間14:30公布決策。先前收緊政策後，市場預期利率維持在4.35%。理事會如何看待油價下跌及通膨二輪效應，將決定其是否認為近期能源壓力緩解足以支持較長時間暫停升息。

美國6月16日美東時間08:30將公布進出口價格及5月房市數據。4月進口價格上漲1.9%，出口價格上漲3.3%，下一次數據將直接檢驗商品價格衝擊是否已擴大。新屋開工前值為年率146.5萬戶，營建許可為142.3萬戶；市場預期開工放緩至143萬戶，許可則微升至142.8萬戶。

美國財政部將於美東時間11:30標售$650億42天期國庫券，6月18日交割、7月30日到期。13:00則將增額發行$130億、票面利率5.000%的20年期公債，2046年5月15日到期，6月22日交割。長債未能跟上週一漲勢，交易量又大幅增加，使這次增額發行成為聯準會決策前，對最終投資人需求及交易商承接能力的直接考驗。

5月零售銷售將於6月17日美東時間08:30公布。市場預期整體銷售增長0.4%，低於4月的0.5%；扣除汽車與汽油後預計增長0.3%，控制組則增長0.4%。若數據穩健，將強化即使工廠數據轉弱，聯準會仍可優先處理通膨的論點；若表現疲弱，需求放緩的證據將更廣泛，市場也會更加重視實質殖利率的下降。

FOMC將於美東時間14:00公布決策及經濟預測摘要，Warsh隨後於14:30舉行記者會。相較預期維持利率在3.50%至3.75%，政策傾向、通膨預測及利率預測分布更為重要。市場將評估官員是否取消先前的寬鬆傾向、是否預測2026年升息，或明確讓下一步取決於油價下降能否傳導至更廣泛的價格。

英國將於6月17日稍早公布消費者物價。市場預期整體通膨率由2.8%升至3.0%，月增率則在前值0.7%後降至0.4%。數據公布後，英格蘭銀行將於6月18日決策，市場預期利率維持3.75%。表決分布與政策指引必須在未來能源壓力降低、家庭通膨預期與近期產出疲弱之間取得平衡。

歐元區6月17日也將公布最終通膨數據，預期整體通膨維持初值3.2%，核心通膨為2.5%。若數字修正，將影響歐洲央行內部的辯論：一方主張提前完成下一次升息，另一方則希望有更多時間評估能源通膨是否正擴散至薪資與服務價格。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries finished June 15 with only modest gains after an interim US-Iran agreement sent oil sharply lower and initially pulled policy-sensitive yields down more decisively. The 2-year yield ended 1.3 basis points lower at 4.069%, the 5-year fell 1.5 basis points to 4.192% and the 10-year declined 0.6 basis point to 4.475%. The 30-year moved in the opposite direction, rising 1.2 basis points to 4.98%, leaving 2s30s 2.5 basis points steeper at 91.1 basis points.

The restrained close obscured a larger intraday repricing. The 2-year yield had fallen as much as 7 basis points to 4.01%, while the 10-year reached 4.42%, as traders reduced the probability of a Federal Reserve increase by December to less than 80% from fully priced during the previous week. Both yields subsequently retraced most of those moves as investors distinguished the immediate decline in crude from the agreement’s still-uncertain implementation and the inflation already working through the economy.

The US and Iran said they had reached an interim accord to halt the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with a formal signing scheduled for June 19 in Switzerland and 60 days of negotiations to follow on Tehran’s nuclear program. WTI closed 4.87% lower at $80.75 and Brent fell 4.76% to $83.17. That reduced the prospective energy impulse confronting central banks, but neither side released an agreed text, shipping had not normalized and Iran attached conditions involving frozen funds, sanctions and the naval blockade.

US data strengthened the case for waiting at this week’s Fed meeting without providing an inflation all-clear. The Empire State manufacturing index fell to 5.7 in June from 19.6, well below expectations of 12.5 to 14.0, and May industrial production rose only 0.1%, missing the 0.2% consensus. Manufacturing output was flat rather than rising the expected 0.3%. Yet the regional survey’s prices-paid index remained elevated at 61.0, supply availability deteriorated and manufacturers expected faster increases in selling prices over the coming 6 months.

That combination helped explain why the Treasury rally faded despite cheaper oil. The 10-year real yield fell 1.4 basis points to 2.137%, but the 10-year breakeven rose 0.8 basis point to 2.338%. The nominal decline therefore came from lower inflation-adjusted yields rather than a fresh collapse in longer-term inflation compensation. The long end also resisted the rally, producing a modest bear-steepening beyond 10 years even as the front end priced less urgency for a Fed increase.

Risk assets responded more forcefully to the removal of the immediate worst-case energy scenario. The S&P 500 rose 1.65%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 3.06% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index jumped 5.45%. The VIX fell 8.37% to 16.2, while the dollar index slipped 0.12%. Credit markets were open for heavy issuance, led by Nvidia’s $25 billion bond sale, which drew as much as $85 billion of orders. The contrast was central to the session: the agreement supported risk taking and reduced near-term tightening pressure, but it did not persuade Treasury investors that the inflation shock or its policy consequences had been fully reversed.

## The Hormuz Agreement Removes a Tail Risk, Not the Implementation Risk

The diplomatic announcement altered the forward energy outlook more than it settled the underlying dispute. The interim agreement is intended to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and stop the fighting, while deferring the nuclear question to a 60-day negotiating period. US and Iranian officials are due to sign the accord in Switzerland on June 19, the date President Donald Trump said the strait would reopen after mines were removed.

The market response reflected the importance of that waterway to global energy supply. Before the war, Hormuz handled about a fifth of seaborne oil and liquefied-natural-gas shipments and about a third of fertilizer exports. Its closure produced a supply shock that lifted inflation readings, shipping costs and expectations for central-bank tightening across both developed and emerging economies. Reopening it offers a direct route toward lower crude prices, reduced import costs and less pressure on headline inflation.

The operational obstacles remain substantial. Almost 600 vessels were reported stranded in the Persian Gulf, with hundreds more waiting outside. Mine clearance alone could take as long as 30 days, and damaged energy infrastructure may delay the recovery in supply even after navigation resumes. Tehran has said ships using the strait would be regulated jointly by Iran and Oman, indicating that Iranian control over passage remains part of the negotiation rather than a fully resolved issue.

The two governments also presented different accounts of what must happen before the broader talks advance. Iran’s semi-official Mehr news agency reported that final negotiations would not begin until half of the country’s frozen funds had been released, oil sanctions suspended and the naval blockade lifted. Sanctions relief could require congressional approval in the US. Tehran has also sought to connect the ceasefire to Israel’s conflict with Hezbollah in Lebanon, adding another condition outside the immediate bilateral dispute.

Those unresolved terms explain why the rates move was much smaller at the close than at its intraday extreme. Lower crude reduced the expected need for aggressive developed-market tightening, but the agreement remains a framework whose inflation effect depends on physical shipping, energy supply and political compliance. Trump has said military attacks could resume if the nuclear negotiations fail, while Iranian hardliners and Israeli opposition create additional paths through which the arrangement could break down.

The completed Treasury curve captured that conditional relief. Shorter maturities outperformed because the immediate change was a reduction in the perceived probability of a Fed increase. The 2-year yield fell to 4.01% early before closing at 4.069%, and the 5-year led the daily-history decline among the main coupon tenors. The 10-year finished only 0.6 basis point lower, while the 30-year rose.

The 2s10s curve steepened 0.7 basis point to 40.6 basis points and 2s30s widened 2.5 basis points to 91.1 basis points. The pattern did not suggest a renewed long-duration flight to safety. Instead, investors reduced some policy-tightening premium at the front while continuing to demand compensation at the long end for residual inflation, supply and term risk.

Treasury cash activity was substantial during the repricing. FINRA recorded $972.1 billion of par activity across 319,747 trades, 8.9% more than on June 12. Nominal-coupon activity increased 3.6% to $760.4 billion. Activity in maturities longer than 20 years rose 35% to $84.1 billion, while the sector above 5 and through 7 years increased 25.3% to $64.4 billion. The figures do not establish investor direction, but they show that the modest closing move followed meaningful turnover, particularly in the maturity sectors that expressed the day’s tension between lower policy risk and persistent long-end resistance.

The cross-asset response was more unequivocally optimistic. Technology led the equity advance, and high-yield and emerging-market bond funds rose modestly. Gold nevertheless gained 2.68% to $4,328, indicating that demand for defensive assets did not disappear alongside the equity rally. The dollar’s small decline was consistent with reduced haven demand, but it was restrained compared with the moves in oil and technology shares.

The agreement therefore changed the distribution of outcomes rather than closing the geopolitical story. It removed some probability from continued severe disruption and gave central banks more latitude to wait. It did not establish how quickly energy flows will normalize, whether sanctions relief will arrive or whether 60 days will be sufficient to settle the nuclear dispute. For bonds, the next phase turns on whether a sharp drop in futures prices becomes a sustained reduction in delivered energy and broader inflation.

## Softer Production Meets Persistent Price Pressure Before the Fed

The June Empire State survey delivered a clear loss of manufacturing momentum. The headline general-business-conditions index fell to 5.7 from 19.6, undershooting the expected range of 12.5 to 14.0. New orders slowed to 3.5 from 22.7 and shipments declined to 8.6 from 18.9, showing that the weaker headline reflected a broad moderation in current activity rather than a single component.

Employment provided a counterpoint. The number-of-employees index rose to 9.6 from 8.3, indicating that firms continued to add workers even as orders and shipments slowed. Expectations also remained positive: the 6-month business-conditions index eased only to 30.1 from 33.5. The survey pointed to slower growth, not an outright manufacturing contraction.

Its price and supply measures were less comfortable for the Fed. Prices paid edged down to 61.0 from 62.6 but remained high, and prices received slipped only to 31.4 from 31.8. Supply availability deteriorated to minus 13.9 from minus 10.7. More importantly for the forward inflation signal, expected prices received over the next 6 months rose to 51.6 from 43.6.

May industrial production reinforced the softer activity message. Total output increased 0.1% on the month, below the 0.2% consensus, after April was revised upward to a 0.9% gain from 0.7%. Production was 1.7% higher from a year earlier. The monthly weakness was concentrated in manufacturing, which was unchanged after a revised 0.7% April increase and missed the expectation for a 0.3% gain.

The sector composition prevented the report from becoming an unambiguous signal of broad weakness. Mining output rose 1.3%, business equipment increased 0.6% and construction supplies advanced 1.1%, while utilities fell 0.4%. Capacity utilization increased to the expected 76.2% from 76.1%, and manufacturing utilization held at 75.7%. The economy was producing below the anticipated monthly pace, but the utilization data did not show a sudden expansion in slack.

Taken together, the releases gave the Fed a reason to observe rather than act immediately. Growth momentum was less forceful than the May employment report and earlier spending figures had suggested, while the retreat in oil improved the prospective headline-inflation path. At the same time, elevated prices paid, deteriorating supply availability and rising expected selling prices showed why policymakers cannot infer from slower output that the inflation problem has ended.

Market pricing moved in that direction. Traders reduced the probability of a quarter-point increase by December to about 74%, and a full move was not priced until March 2027. UBS strategist Leslie Falconio said the decline in oil was allowing the market to remove some of the hikes it had added, helping the 2-year yield fall. She nevertheless expected the FOMC to remove its easing bias this week, while continuing to forecast that the next actual rate change would be a cut in 2027.

The distinction between the immediate decision and the policy bias is important. A hold at 3.50%-3.75% is widely expected at Kevin Warsh’s first meeting as Fed chair. The incoming evidence makes an increase this week unlikely, but it leaves the committee deciding whether to signal that the next move could occur in either direction. Lower oil reduces the need for urgent tightening; sticky survey prices and still-resilient capacity use argue against restoring an explicit preference for easing.

The Treasury bill auctions supplied a separate front-end demand signal. The $89.001 billion 13-week sale stopped at a 3.640% high rate, unchanged from the previous week. Its bid-to-cover ratio fell to 2.47 from 2.79, indirect bidders took 49.81%, direct bidders received 4.77% and primary dealers absorbed 45.42%. The higher dealer allocation accompanied markedly weaker cover, though no when-issued reference was available to characterize the stop itself.

The $77 billion 26-week sale produced a firmer result. It stopped at 3.680%, 1 basis point below the prior week, while bid-to-cover edged up to 2.76 from 2.75. Indirect bidders took 70.11%, direct bidders 6.57% and dealers 23.33%. Both securities settle June 18, but their different demand profiles argue against treating the auctions as one uniform front-end liquidity verdict.

The 13-week result showed weaker absorption at an unchanged rate, while the 26-week sale maintained cover and attracted a much larger indirect share at a slightly lower rate. Neither auction displayed generalized funding stress. Their relevance lies in the segmentation: cash demand was more comfortable at 6 months than at 3 months as investors approached the Fed meeting, the corporate tax date and a dense sequence of Treasury settlements.

## Nvidia’s Jumbo Sale Tests the Depth of AI Credit Demand

Corporate borrowers used the improvement in market sentiment aggressively, with Nvidia providing the session’s defining credit transaction. The chipmaker sold $25 billion of investment-grade bonds in its first offering since 2021, increasing the deal from an initial target of about $20 billion after attracting as much as $85 billion in orders.

The sale was divided into seven maturities ranging from 2 to 30 years. Pricing on the longest tranche tightened by 25 basis points during marketing to 65 basis points over Treasuries. Nvidia completed the transaction without the investor calls that ordinarily precede a large high-grade offering, reflecting its dominant market position, strong credit ratings and scarcity as a bond issuer.

The company’s financial profile distinguished it from more leveraged AI infrastructure borrowers. Nvidia is expected to generate more than $200 billion of free cash flow in the fiscal year ending January 31, according to the average analyst estimate. It is also a major supplier to the data-center expansion that is driving borrowing by Alphabet, Amazon and other technology companies, while deploying capital of its own through investments in Intel, Anthropic and OpenAI.

Proceeds are intended partly to refinance outstanding debt. The relatively inexpensive long-dated funding can also support strategic investments and shareholder distributions without materially weakening Nvidia’s AA credit profile. Investors were therefore financing both a large capital-allocation program and a company with exceptional internal cash generation.

The wider market showed similar capacity. Eight investment-grade issuers raised a combined $36 billion on Monday. A measure of investment-grade credit risk fell to its lowest level since early February, before the Iran conflict began, and US high-grade bond funds had recorded 13 consecutive months of inflows. The combination of lower oil, modestly lower Treasury yields and persistent fund demand created an unusually supportive issuance window.

That capacity does not eliminate concentration risk. Nvidia’s offering joins hundreds of billions of dollars of technology borrowing directed toward data centers and other AI infrastructure. Morgan Stanley’s head of debt capital markets estimated that as much as 15% of all credit issuance this year could be related to AI, even though the category barely existed 2 years ago.

The shift is beginning to appear in macro balance sheets as well as primary-market calendars. Bespoke Investment Group found that the amount of debt growth associated with each unit of US gross-domestic-product growth had increased during the past year, with corporate borrowing central to the change. AI investment helps explain why economic growth, imports and bond issuance have all become more credit-intensive. The financing can support output before the eventual productivity gains arrive, but it increases the importance of whether those gains are sufficient to service the new capital.

Nuveen’s Laura Parrott described a more selective approach inside her roughly $75 billion investment-grade portfolio. She has focused on energy and utility credits that provide power, transmission and other infrastructure around AI rather than relying solely on the technology’s eventual commercial winners. She also warned that circular relationships among hyperscalers, model developers and infrastructure providers can leave portfolios with more exposure to one underlying borrower than transaction labels suggest.

Other primary deals demonstrated that demand extended beyond US technology. Montreal’s Réseau express métropolitain raised C$1.85 billion across 5-, 7-, 10- and 30-year maturities. The 30-year tranche priced 95 basis points over government bonds to yield 4.791% and drew orders exceeding 5 times its size. The financing allows capital previously committed to the light-rail project to be redeployed, although the system is not expected to be fully operational until its airport connection opens in 2027 and estimated project costs have almost doubled to C$9.4 billion since 2015.

Waste Management of Canada sold C$700 million of 7-year notes at 72 basis points over government debt, 3 basis points tighter than initial pricing. Birkenstock prepared a separate €900 million, 7-year bond callable after 3 years, its first sale since 2021. The footwear company plans to refinance debt and could use as much as $500 million for additional share repurchases, following a $250 million accelerated buyback.

The benign issuance backdrop also allowed the World Bank’s private-sector arm to expand a less conventional funding structure. The International Finance Corp. raised $509 million through its second emerging-market collateralized-loan obligation in less than a year, taking the program above $1 billion. The transaction bundles 62 dollar-denominated loans from South America, the Middle East, North Africa and Asia.

Its $320 million senior tranche received a provisional Aaa rating from Moody’s and priced at 120 basis points over SOFR, 10 basis points tighter than the comparable tranche in the IFC’s first deal. The structure transfers part of the lender’s risk to bond investors and releases capital for new loans, while giving buyers diversified emerging-market exposure. Its tighter pricing provides a direct indication of greater investor familiarity with the structure.

The same market strength is drawing increased supervisory attention to less transparent credit channels. The European Central Bank has expanded its review of bank links to private credit to more than 20 institutions from about a dozen. Banks with meaningful exposure will have to supply information annually, with officials focusing not only on the amount lent but also on overlapping exposures across funds, portfolio companies and co-lending arrangements.

Deutsche Bank, Barclays, BNP Paribas and HSBC account for almost two-thirds of European bank exposure to private credit, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. Disclosed exposures amount to about 2.3% of loans, suggesting a manageable aggregate size, but ECB supervisors are concerned that inadequate aggregation could obscure concentrations and correlations during stress. The review is particularly relevant after private-credit funds imposed withdrawal limits and investor confidence weakened.

The result is a credit market with abundant current demand but growing structural concentration. Nvidia could raise more than originally planned and tighten pricing substantially because investors viewed its balance sheet, scarcity and role in the AI ecosystem as unusually strong. The ECB’s review and Nuveen’s concentration concerns address the other side of the same financing boom: large volumes can be absorbed without immediate spread stress while still creating interconnected exposures that become visible only when growth, liquidity or the expected AI payoff disappoints.

## Europe Balances Weak Output Against Energy’s Second-Round Effects

European rates also benefited from the decline in oil, but central-bank officials resisted the conclusion that cheaper futures had reversed the inflation already moving through the economy. ECB President Christine Lagarde said indirect effects from high energy prices had begun to appear broadly and identified underlying inflation and wage pressure as the indicators that would determine whether further action was required.

The ECB raised its deposit rate by 25 basis points the previous week, its first increase since 2023. Money markets still priced another quarter-point increase to 2.5% by year-end, but reduced the chance of a further move to 2.75% to about 25%, from fully priced during the prior week. The repricing recognized that a durable Hormuz reopening would reduce the need for a rapid sequence without erasing the effects of the preceding shock.

Lagarde welcomed the prospective agreement while making its implementation conditional on developments in the coming days, a signed memorandum and actual reopening and de-mining of the strait. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel warned that oil supplies could take months to normalize and that inflation pressure might rise again as fiscal support for energy bills expires.

Other Governing Council members differed on the required pace. Portugal’s Alvaro Santos Pereira said it was too early to infer a policy path before officials knew whether inflation would spread from energy and fertilizers into other sectors. Slovakia’s Peter Kazimir favored front-loading the remaining work, arguing that the economic damage from the war could not be undone immediately. Latvia’s Martins Kazaks said the ECB was prepared to act again if higher energy prices continued to spread.

The growth data strengthen the case for caution. Euro-area industrial production rose 0.1% in April, below the 0.2% monthly consensus, after a 0.4% March increase. Output was 0.3% above its year-earlier level, compared with an expected 0.4%. Intermediate goods increased 0.8%, durable consumer goods 1.0% and non-durable consumer goods 1.7%, but energy output fell 0.4% and capital goods declined 0.5%.

The composition suggests that consumer-related production held up while the capital-goods sector remained weak. Across the broader European Union, output rose 0.1% on the month and 0.9% from a year earlier. The data do not point to an abrupt industrial contraction, but they leave the euro area with limited growth momentum as higher energy costs move beyond their initial source.

European credit faces the same tension. Deutsche Bank strategists favor US dollar corporate bonds over euro credit because they expect the war’s aftereffects to weigh more heavily on European issuers through sticky inflation, higher shipping costs, memory-chip shortages and tariff uncertainty. They forecast euro investment-grade spreads widening by almost 20 basis points to 95 basis points by year-end and euro high-yield spreads increasing 77 basis points to 345.

Their US forecasts are less severe: a 10-basis-point widening to 82 basis points for investment-grade bonds and 39 basis points for high yield. The strategists see European single-B companies as particularly exposed because 44% would move into negative free cash flow if total funding costs rose by 0.5 percentage point. The comparison does not imply immediate market stress, but it highlights why a lower oil price may provide less durable relief in Europe when growth is softer and refinancing capacity is weaker.

Poland’s policy debate shifted in a less hawkish direction without returning to an easing commitment. Monetary Policy Council member Ludwik Kotecki said rates were likely to remain at 3.75% through at least year-end and possibly until March 2027, when base effects should lower annual inflation. The council had paused its cutting cycle after the war lifted energy prices.

Kotecki said the interim agreement reduced the likelihood of another increase, particularly after Polish inflation slowed to 3.1% in May. He nevertheless rejected signaling a near-term return to cuts. Even if inflation rises when the government removes its fuel-price cap, he described that prospective increase as administrative and said core pressure remained low. His position places Poland between the ECB’s active tightening debate and central banks able to ease immediately.

Zimbabwe became the first central bank to cut rates following the US-Iran announcement, lowering its benchmark to 30% from 35%. Governor John Mushayavanhu described the decision as a realignment to a structural change in inflation rather than the start of an easing cycle. Annual inflation slowed to 4.4% in May from 4.8% in April and had fallen from 95.8% in July 2025. The central bank expects resumed oil and fertilizer flows to reinforce that decline, but kept the distinction between a one-time adjustment and a sustained sequence.

Brazil moved in the opposite direction. Economists raised their year-end Selic forecast to 13.75% from 13.5%, even after policymakers had delivered consecutive quarter-point cuts to 14.5%. The same survey lifted the end-2027 estimate to 12% from 11.5% and the end-2028 forecast to 10.25% from 10%.

Expected inflation for 2026 rose to 5.3% from 5.11%, above both the central bank’s 3% goal and the 4.5% upper edge of its tolerance range. Fiscal support before the October election, a weaker real and potential El Niño effects are sustaining price risks despite the global decline in oil. The evidence leaves investors questioning whether the central bank has room to continue easing after its coming decision.

## Sovereign Funding and Asian Liquidity Keep Domestic Risks in View

The improvement in global risk appetite opened financing opportunities for lower-rated sovereign and quasi-sovereign borrowers, but domestic fiscal and liquidity conditions remained decisive. Kenya plans to sell a $1.13 billion foreign bond during the fiscal year beginning in July as part of a 529 billion-shilling external-borrowing program to finance a deficit equal to 5.5% of gross domestic product.

The bond, a World Bank development-policy loan and African Development Bank financing are expected to provide almost two-thirds of Kenya’s external funding. The Treasury anticipates disbursements of 170.5 billion shillings from the World Bank and 21.3 billion shillings from the African lender. Kenya is classified by the International Monetary Fund as being at high risk of debt distress, and lawmakers have warned that continued borrowing for both budget expenditure and refinancing is adding to future fiscal pressure.

The prospective sale follows a $2.25 billion dual-tranche transaction in February, a $3 billion market operation in 2025 and a $1.5 billion, 6-year Eurobond in 2024. Those deals have extended maturities and eased near-term external liquidity pressure, but the new issue would continue the pattern of using market access partly to manage existing debt.

Scotland is preparing a different sovereign-style debut. Its devolved government plans to issue bonds in the fourth quarter of 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, beginning a £1.5 billion program over 5 years. The transaction would replace some borrowing from the central UK government with direct market funding.

The main pricing question is how investors will treat the possibility of eventual Scottish independence. S&P and Moody’s assigned Scotland the same rating as the UK under the existing constitutional structure, but both made clear that the assessment depends on Scotland remaining in the union. Investors are focused on whether the bonds would continue to be repaid in sterling and whether documentation would provide early redemption if independence occurred.

The current assumption presented to banks is that the securities will contain no special covenant for material political events. Comparable references offer a wide range: an Isle of Man bond trades more than 50 basis points above similar gilts, while a Lancashire County Council note due in 2060 carries a premium near 70 basis points. The eventual maturity may matter as much as the issuer’s current rating because a 30-year bond would carry much more exposure to constitutional change than a 5-year issue.

Taiwan’s government-bond market presented a more immediate liquidity problem. The island’s 5-year yields were near their highest since 2008 and 10-year yields close to a 3-year peak as tax payments, inflation concerns and loan demand from brokerages tightened cash conditions. Brokerages have been borrowing to finance participation in the AI-led stock-market advance, adding to the pressure on bank liquidity.

Outstanding central-bank certificates of deposit have fallen to NT$6.15 trillion, the lowest since June 2010, as lenders conserve cash rather than purchase additional paper. Demand at government auctions has also weakened, and the previous week’s 10-year sale produced the highest yield since 2013. Governor Yang Chin-long attributed the decline in bond and certificate demand to tax payments, AI-company funding needs and the stock-market boom.

Taiwan’s central bank is expected to hold its policy rate at 2% on June 18, but investors will watch whether May inflation above the bank’s alert level changes its guidance. Lower global oil gives officials some room to wait, while existing market rates are already restraining demand. Analysts at BNP Paribas raised the possibility of a gradual adjustment that guides the overnight interbank rate closer to the policy rate, potentially cooling speculative borrowing without an immediate increase in the benchmark.

The Bank of Japan faces a different communication challenge at the end of its June 15-16 meeting. A 25-basis-point increase from about 0.75% to 1% is widely expected, which would take the key rate to its highest since 1995. Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida will explain the decision because Governor Kazuo Ueda remains hospitalized and will submit views in writing without voting.

Uchida must address both the subsequent rate path and the BOJ’s bond purchases. The bank is expected to announce that it will stop reducing purchases from April 2027, an important change in the normalization program. A forceful rate signal could support the yen but add pressure to a JGB market already struggling to attract reliable super-long buyers; a cautious message could revive concern that inflation and currency weakness are outrunning policy.

The session’s broad lesson outside the US was that cheaper oil improves the global starting point but does not impose a single rates outcome. Zimbabwe had enough disinflation to cut, Poland saw room to wait, Brazil’s fiscal and inflation dynamics reduced its easing space, and Taiwan’s bond pressure came from domestic cash scarcity as well as energy prices. The BOJ is expected to tighten despite the global relief because its normalization, yen and inflation conditions remain distinct.

## Forward Market Significance

Asia’s first tests arrive June 16. China releases May industrial production, retail sales and fixed-asset investment at 10:00 in Shanghai. The previous readings were 4.1% annual industrial growth, 3.2% retail-sales growth and a 1.6% year-to-date contraction in fixed investment. The package will show whether domestic demand is recovering while policymakers contend with weak private borrowing and abundant banking liquidity.

The BOJ decision follows the June 15-16 meeting, with a 25-basis-point increase to around 1% expected. The rate move is heavily anticipated, placing more weight on Uchida’s account of future increases and the plan for bond purchases. Confirmation that the BOJ will stop reducing purchases from April 2027 could support market functioning, but investors will also assess whether that decision changes the pace of monetary normalization.

The Reserve Bank of Australia announces its decision at 14:30 Sydney time. A hold at 4.35% is expected after earlier tightening. Its treatment of the oil decline and second-round inflation risk will determine whether the Board regards the latest energy relief as sufficient to pause for an extended period.

US import and export prices and May housing data arrive at 08:30 ET on June 16. April import prices rose 1.9% and export prices 3.3%, making the next release a direct test of whether the goods-price impulse has broadened. Housing starts previously ran at a 1.465 million annualized rate, while permits were 1.423 million. Expectations call for starts to slow to 1.430 million and permits to edge up to 1.428 million.

Treasury will sell $65 billion of 42-day bills at 11:30 ET, with June 18 settlement and July 30 maturity. At 13:00, it will reopen $13 billion of the 5.000% 20-year bond due May 15, 2046, for June 22 settlement. The long-bond sector resisted Monday’s rally and recorded a large increase in trading activity, making the reopening a direct test of end-user demand and dealer capacity before the Fed decision.

May retail sales arrive June 17 at 08:30 ET. Headline sales are expected to increase 0.4%, compared with a 0.5% April gain, while sales excluding autos and gasoline are expected to rise 0.3% and the control group 0.4%. A resilient result would reinforce the argument that the Fed can prioritize inflation even after softer factory data. A weak report would broaden the evidence of slower demand and place more weight on the decline in real yields.

The FOMC announces its decision and Summary of Economic Projections at 14:00 ET, followed by Warsh’s press conference at 14:30. The expected hold at 3.50%-3.75% is less consequential than the policy bias, inflation projections and distribution of rate forecasts. Markets will assess whether officials remove their previous easing preference, show increases during 2026 or leave the next move explicitly dependent on whether lower oil feeds through to broader prices.

UK consumer prices are released earlier on June 17. Headline inflation is expected to rise to 3.0% from 2.8%, with a 0.4% monthly increase after 0.7%. The result precedes the Bank of England’s June 18 decision, where a hold at 3.75% is expected. The vote split and guidance must reconcile lower prospective energy pressure with household inflation expectations and weak recent output.

Euro-area final inflation figures are also due June 17, with headline inflation expected to remain at the 3.2% flash estimate and core inflation at 2.5%. A revision would affect the debate between ECB officials who favor front-loading another increase and those who want more time to evaluate whether energy inflation is spreading into wages and services.

June 18 brings decisions from Bank Indonesia, the Swiss National Bank, Norges Bank, the Bank of England and the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. Indonesia and the Philippines are each expected to consider another 25-basis-point increase, while the SNB and BOE are expected to hold. Norges Bank’s new rate path will show whether its May increase is followed by a pause. The common energy shock has receded, but currency pressure, domestic inflation and wage growth leave those policy decisions far from uniform.

US initial jobless claims on June 18 will test whether the recent rise to 229,000 new claims and 1.795 million continuing claims persists. Treasury will then reopen $24 billion of 1.250% 5-year inflation-protected securities at 13:00, with June 30 settlement and April 15, 2031 maturity. The auction follows the Fed projections and will offer a direct test of demand for real yield and inflation protection after the 10-year breakeven rose even as oil fell.

The US fixed-income market is scheduled for a full Juneteenth close on June 19, the same day US and Iranian officials are due to sign the interim agreement in Switzerland. That timing compresses domestic price discovery after the Fed, BOE, global policy decisions and Treasury supply. The more durable rates signal will come from whether the agreement produces mine clearance, resumed vessel traffic and sustained energy flows—not simply another declaration that Hormuz will reopen.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury rally fades as Hormuz relief lowers near-term policy risk but leaves the long end under pressure
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries finished June 15 with modest gains after an interim US-Iran agreement to halt the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz sent oil sharply lower. The 2-year yield fell 1.3 basis points to 4.069%, the 5-year declined 1.5 basis points to 4.192% and the 10-year slipped 0.6 basis point to 4.475%, while the 30-year rose 1.2 basis points to 4.98%. The resulting 2s30s curve steepened 2.5 basis points to 91.1 basis points.

The close retraced a larger initial rally in which the 2-year reached 4.01% and the 10-year 4.42%. Cheaper crude reduced expectations for near-term tightening, but investors remained wary because no agreed text had been released, shipping had not normalized and the accord still depended on mine clearance, sanctions negotiations and political compliance. The 10-year real yield fell 1.4 basis points to 2.137%, while the 10-year breakeven rose 0.8 basis point to 2.338%, showing that the nominal rally came from lower real yields rather than a broad retreat in longer-term inflation compensation.

US factory data reinforced the case for the Fed to wait without delivering an inflation all-clear. The Empire State index fell to 5.7, May industrial production rose only 0.1% and manufacturing output was flat, but prices paid remained elevated at 61.0 and expected selling-price increases accelerated. Risk assets responded more strongly to the reduced energy tail risk: technology shares rallied, volatility fell and heavy credit issuance was absorbed, including Nvidia’s $25 billion bond sale. The next test is whether the June 19 signing produces actual vessel traffic and sustained energy flows, while the Fed’s June 17 guidance clarifies whether lower oil changes its policy bias.
